title: Agent Atlas
description: A seed literature taxonomy of agent improvement mechanisms and research evidence.
coverage: Eight representative papers, not a comprehensive review.
annotation_kind: Editorial summaries of cited papers; not independent replications.
relationship_semantics: Branch parent_id expresses taxonomy. Paper branch_ids express classification. Neither represents actual paper ancestry or agent-version lineage.

question_filter.meaning: Highlight mechanism-relevant work. Exclusion does not mean evidence of absence.

status_definitions.tested: Tested within the specific experimental scope in the note; not a general proof.
status_definitions.mechanism: The mechanism is present or provides indirect support; the research question is not fully isolated.
status_definitions.unknown: The atlas has not verified evidence for this question; not evidence of absence.
status_definitions.outside: Outside the core method's stated scope.

questions.title: Can capabilities be inherited?
questions.description: Track what experience is retained and whether it remains useful in descendants, other tasks, or different models.
questions.criterion: Transfer evaluations, component transplants, removal studies, and rollback experiments.

questions.title: Can lineage improve search?
questions.description: Distinguish recording history from using ancestors, branches, and failed attempts to choose the next modification.
questions.criterion: Equal-budget comparisons with linear improvement and ordinary archive search.

questions.title: Do descendants become better improvers?
questions.description: Distinguish higher task scores, an editable improver, and measured gains in the ability to produce useful changes.
questions.criterion: Compare ancestors and descendants under the same future search budget.

all.title: Agent improvement
all.summary: Representative papers organized by improvement mechanism. Taxonomy links are classifications, not claims about actual ancestry.

harness.title: Harness improvement
harness.summary: Improve the system around a model: prompts, tools, memory, skills, and agent code. Mechanisms may overlap.

evolution.title: Archive search & branch evolution
evolution.summary: Use prior candidates or selected parents to generate, evaluate, and retain new agents. Actual version inheritance is a harness improvement mechanism within this branch.

iterative.title: Iterative optimization
iterative.summary: Turn evaluation feedback into updates to prompts, code, and other variables in the current system.

memory.title: Experience accumulation
memory.summary: Retain experience as retrievable reflections or code skills for reuse in later attempts and tasks.

joint.title: Model–harness co-optimization
joint.summary: Compilation and optimization may target both a language-model pipeline and learnable model parameters. Fine-tuning is optional; evidence depends on the configuration.

foundation.title: Related foundations
foundation.summary: Foundational methods that help define the scope of self-improvement. Revising an output within a task does not establish persistent agent capability growth.

papers.name: DGM
papers.title: Darwin Gödel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
papers.mechanism: Select a parent agent from a historical archive, modify its code, and evaluate the resulting variant on coding tasks.

q1.note: Descendants inherit code, and designs were tested across models. The causal contribution of individual inherited capabilities still requires separate tests.

q2.note: Archive exploration was compared with linear updates and greedy parent selection. Evidence covers the archive and parent-selection strategies.

q3.note: Improved agents continue self-modification, with a fixed initial-improver baseline. General gains in improvement efficiency require further validation.

papers.name: Hyperagents
papers.title: Hyperagents
papers.mechanism: Place the task agent and its modifying meta agent in one editable program, allowing the mechanism that generates future improvements to evolve.

q1.note: Meta-level improvements were tested for cross-domain transfer and cross-run reuse. Not every inherited component received a causal ablation.

q2.note: Open-ended archive exploration baselines were compared. The independent benefit of lineage-depth selection remains to be verified.

q3.note: Section 5.2 freezes a transferred meta agent and measures its ability to generate better agents using imp@50.

papers.limitation: Some final cross-run differences were not statistically significant. The results do not establish universal or unbounded self-acceleration.

papers.name: ADAS
papers.title: Automated Design of Agentic Systems
papers.mechanism: A meta agent programs new agents using an expanding archive of candidates and feeds evaluation results into the next design round.

q1.note: Whole designs were tested across domains and models. This does not isolate the causal effect of component inheritance.

q2.note: The candidate archive informs search. This differs from isolating the value of explicit parent–child lineage.

q3.note: The meta-level process in Meta Agent Search remains fixed.

papers.name: Reflexion
papers.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
papers.mechanism: Convert task feedback into verbal reflections stored in episodic memory for later attempts, without updating model weights.

q1.note: Reflective memory was tested for its benefit on later attempts. This does not establish inheritance between independent descendants.

q2.note: The core method does not search a parent–child agent-version lineage.

q3.note: A fixed framework executes reflection and update steps.

papers.name: Voyager
papers.title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
papers.mechanism: Improve programs using Minecraft environment feedback and store successful behaviors in a retrievable, composable code-skill library.

q1.note: Learned skills were transferred to a new world to solve new tasks. The evidence concerns skill reuse.

q2.note: Skill retrieval and composition do not depend on parent–child version-lineage search.

q3.note: The skill-generation and improvement framework remains fixed.

papers.name: TextGrad
papers.title: TextGrad: Automatic “Differentiation” via Text
papers.mechanism: Backpropagate language-model-generated textual feedback through a computation graph to optimize prompts, code, and other system variables.

q1.note: Variable optimization gains were demonstrated. Evidence of descendant capability inheritance has not been verified in this atlas.

q2.note: The computation graph describes feedback propagation, not agent-version ancestry.

q3.note: The original TextGrad uses a predefined optimization framework.

papers.name: DSPy
papers.title: DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines
papers.mechanism: Express language-model pipelines as declarative modules, then compile them by optimizing demonstrations and other learnable parameters against a target metric.

q1.note: Compiled pipeline performance was tested. Module reuse and strict capability inheritance require further distinction.

q2.note: Parent–child agent-lineage search is not the original paper's central contribution.

q3.note: The compilation process does not target autonomous rewriting of its optimizer.

papers.name: Self-Refine
papers.title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
papers.mechanism: Alternate feedback and revision with the same language model to improve the current task output.

q1.note: The study concerns within-task output refinement, not persistent descendant capabilities.

q2.note: The core process is linear refinement, not agent-version lineage search.

q3.note: The feedback and revision procedure remains fixed.
